requirements.requirement: Run a long-running background worker as a managed systemd service named inventory-worker on node1
requirements.summary: Unit file created at /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service, enabled and started via systemctl enable --now; systemctl status shows Active: active (running) with a persistent loop process and sleep child. Tick counter in state.json incremented across polls (tick 1->3->5->7), directly demonstrating continuous long-running operation both before and after a reboot.

requirements.requirement: Service confined so it writes only inside /var/lib/inventory
requirements.summary: Unit uses ProtectSystem=strict with ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory only. Directory listing shows only state.json/worker.log written there. An empirical probe run as the same user with the same sandbox properties succeeded writing inside /var/lib/inventory but failed with 'Read-only file system' when attempting writes to /tmp and /etc, directly confirming the write confinement rather than relying on configuration alone.

systemctl show reports NoNewPrivileges=yes for the unit, and /proc/<MainPID>/status of the actually running process confirms NoNewPrivs:1 at the kernel level, directly verifying the runtime behavior, not just the configured property.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 with pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id 98aa35f5... with service active/enabled and tick=5. Reboot was triggered via backgrounded nohup and returned 'reboot-scheduled' before the connection dropped. Node was unreachable during the transition (connection reset then timeouts), then reachable again with a different boot_id (187948fa...), confirming a genuine kernel restart. Post-reboot state shows service active/enabled with a new MainPID, and state.json/worker.log persisted with the tick counter resuming (5->7), demonstrating full recovery. This is corroborated independently by the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshot, which also shows the boot id change from 98aa35f5... to 187948fa...

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task were directly and empirically verified: inventory-worker runs as an enabled systemd service continuously ticking, is confined to /var/lib/inventory (proven by a failed-write probe to /tmp and /etc), and runs with NoNewPrivs confirmed at the kernel level. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also fully and coherently demonstrated with a pre-restart baseline, a real reboot (boot_id change corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots), and confirmed post-reboot recovery of both the service and its data. The only shortcoming is minor unreverted residue (/tmp/probe.out, /tmp/reboot.log) from diagnostic probes, which is low-risk and does not affect task functionality.
limitations: Minor temp-file residue (/tmp/probe.out, /tmp/reboot.log) from executor diagnostics was left on node1 and not cleaned up, though it poses no security or functional risk.

The initial confinement probe (cmd-e90bde80debe47b3) failed with return_code 208, likely due to --pty in a non-interactive execution context; this was a benign retry rather than a task failure, as the follow-up probe succeeded and produced the definitive confinement evidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: The executor's state-changing commands were largely purposeful: user/group creation, directory setup, script and unit creation, enabling the service, and cleanup of the temporary probe.txt file inside /var/lib/inventory (cmd-5fc1b89a67744240) all map directly to satisfying the task or collecting bounded evidence. Two ephemeral confinement-verification probes (cmd-e90bde80debe47b3, cmd-67455cdfc7b34f38) were reasonable, low-risk, bounded diagnostic actions tied to demonstrating the write-confinement requirement; the first failed harmlessly (return_code 208, likely due to --pty in a non-interactive session) and was superseded by the second, successful probe. However, residue from these probes — /tmp/probe.out and /tmp/reboot.log — remained on the node per the after_executor temporary-files snapshot and were not cleaned up, and the probe2 systemd unit required a reset-failed call. This is minor, non-sensitive, low-risk leftover state rather than a broad or destructive mutation, but it was not fully restored.
